text:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered -> PD INC-8421: high LB target failure rate (eu-west-1). Symptoms: TLS handshake failures from ALB to backend targets. Auto-page to on-call. https://pagerduty.example/INC8421 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-8421 auto-escalated to second level (10m unacked). Current status: triggered -> acknowledged pending owner.

sara: acked. I'm on it, will do initial blast-radius check and blast the team. Anyone recently touched eu-west DNS weights or LB config?

mike: not me. Just saw the page. I'm checking target group health now.

alex: quick note — we rolled a small weighted DNS change to shift 8% traffic to eu-west about 18m ago for canary. Could be related.

mike: doing describe-target-health -> there are a bunch of 502/SSL_HANDSHAKE failures. Copying snippet:

```
> aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --region eu-west-1
TargetHealthDescriptions:
  - Id: ip-10-0-5-12.ec2.internal
    HealthCheckPort: 443
    TargetHealth:
      State: unhealthy
      Reason: TLS handshake failure
```

mike: curl to backend private IP shows TLS alert: "handshake failure". Trying openssl s_client for SNI details.

alex: running openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername app.internal shows certificate SANs: [app.internal, staging.internal], issuer = OurTestCA, not the prod cert. That explains hostname mismatch / handshake.

jess: who deployed that build? That cert looks like a staging cert. Might be a bad image pushed to eu-west during a partial rollout.

sara: investigating deploy tracker... looks like an automated canary rollout touched eu-west target group 22m ago. Rollout ID: rollout-2026-06-11-1745.

mike: stepping back: impact assessment? Front door LB is failing to reach some targets, so requests routed to eu-west are seeing 502s. Global traffic % to eu-west is 8 (per alex), so user impact limited but customers in EU are affected intermittently. PD severity currently P1 due to customer errors.

oncall-manager: @sara if it's a bad image/cert, please coordinate rollback. Also notify support for customer comms.

sara: plan: 1) remove unhealthy targets from target-group to stop 502s 2) rollback weighted DNS -> revert 8% back to baseline to stop routing new traffic to eu-west 3) block further rollout jobs to eu-west 4) confirm certificates on backends and redeploy correct image.

mike: removing targets from target-group now (drain=false) so ALB will stop routing. Using:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --targets Id=10.0.5.12 Id=10.0.5.13 --region eu-west-1
```

alex: rolling back DNS weight via Route53 change-set to revert canary: updated weighted record from 8%->0% for eu-west. TTL still low (60s), but propagation may take a minute.

jess: Support notified (message sent) — holding on email templates until we have rollback confirmation.

mike: target deregister command completed. ALB target health now shows fewer unhealthy targets. Live checks show error rate dropping.

incidents-bot: PagerDuty INC-8421 status update: acknowledged by sara. Auto-escalation paused.

sara: can someone verify certificates on the image that was rolled? I pulled the container image manifest: image: registry.redwood.dev/prod/app:2026-06-11-1742 -> that image was accidentally built using staging TLS cert at build-time. We need to remove that tag and mark manifest as bad.

alex: found CI job that injected test cert via env var on build matrix. I'll open a patch to prevent test cert into prod images.

mike: after deregistering targets and rollback of DNS weight, frontend 5xxs dropped from 3.2% -> 0.4% in last 3 minutes. Good signal.

jess: support: pushing interim note to affected customers: "We observed elevated errors for a subset of EU traffic. We've routed traffic away from the affected hosts and are restoring full service." Waiting final confirmation to close PD.

sara: next steps: 1) fix CI to avoid test certs (alex) 2) re-build and promote corrected image to eu-west behind a canary (sized to 2% only) (mike) 3) add a preflight cert check in the rollout job (me) 4) postmortem after incident.

mike: starting rebuild now. Will push image with tag corrected-2026-06-11-1758 and run health checks in a private canary prior to reattaching targets.

pagerduty-bot: INC-8421 updated -> status: resolved (manual resolution) by sara. Resolution note: rolled back DNS weight, removed bad targets, rebuilt image without staging cert, verified health checks.

sara: confirming: frontend error rate normalized across eu-west traffic paths. We'll keep monitoring for 30m. I'll own the postmortem. Assigning to: sara, alex, mike.

oncall-manager: great work. After-action items assigned. Please add timeline + root cause in the postmortem: CI mis-injection of staging cert into prod image + weighted DNS canary amplified exposure.

jess: support sent follow-up to customers and updated incident status page.

sara: closing thread in 30m unless new alerts. Thanks all. :clap:
